title: I rise from scavenger to king with alien tech.
body_text: After World War III, Arthur Morgan is reduced to scraping by in the chaos, surviving on scavenged goods while being bullied and robbed by former high school classmates—until a chance discovery of alien technology changes everything. He rescues three women who become his wives and sets his sights on using this power to rise as the King of the Wasteland.

title: 👆  Read this if the allergies won’t go away
body_text:
Please STOP buying allergy meds for your dog.

I know that sounds insane when you're watching him chew through his own skin at 2am., but hear me out.

Because I'm about to tell you the one thing I figured out about dog allergies that I wish someone had told me 2 years and $3400 dollars ago.

It's the thing that explains why every drug stops working after three weeks. Why every supplement you've tried did nothing. Why your vet keeps adding more medications and your dog is still scratching.

I'm a dog groomer. Sixteen years in this industry. I didn't know it either.

And once you know it, the entire pet allergy industry stops making sense.

His name is Henry. Six year old Cavalier King Charles. My soul pup.

He started itching at two. Just seasonal. By year four it was year-round. By year five he was in the cone permanently. By year six the only thing my husband and I talked about over coffee in the morning was whether Henry made it through the night without tearing himself open.

In twelve months I spent $3400 dollars on him.

I'm going to tell you what that bought me.

NOTHING

Apoquel was first. $156 a month. Worked for three weeks then quit. Vet said increase the dose. I did. It quit again two weeks later.

Then Cytopoint shots. $189 every two weeks. Worked three weeks at a time. By month six we were going in early because the itching was coming back early.

Then Cyclosporine. Until his gums grew over his teeth so thick he couldn't chew kibble.

Then Zenrelia. Worked for fourteen days. Then he was scratching again.

By the fourth drug I knew something was wrong. Not with Henry. With the whole approach.

I just didn't know what yet.

Meanwhile I was running every grooming protocol I knew. Twice weekly chlorhexidine baths. Daily ear cleaning. Paw wipes. Oatmeal soaks. Coconut oil. Apple cider vinegar in his water bowl. Eight different supplements stacked in the cabinet above his food.

The cone wore the fur off the back of his neck.

He chewed his belly through the cone anyway.

One night I sat on the bathroom floor at 2am watching him scrape his face on the bath mat. Something broke. Not loud. Not crying. Just empty.

I grabbed my laptop and started typing things I'd never typed before.

"Why does Apoquel stop working."

"Dog still itching on Cytopoint."

Thousands of dog parents asking the same questions. Same story repeating in the answers: works for a few weeks, stops, vet adds something else, that stops too, dog still scratching.

Then I found one thread that wasn't like the others. Where everyone else was venting, one vet had actually answered.

What she wrote changed everything for me. I screenshotted it and read it back to myself five times.

"Allergies compromise the skin barrier, and then the microbes get in and set up infection. If you don't address the underlying cause AND the secondary infection, the allergy meds will not work."

The skin barrier.

Sixteen years grooming and I'd never heard those two words used together. Not from my vet. Not from the dermatologist. Not from any product I'd ever sold in my own salon.

So I went down the rabbit hole. And what I found explained every single failure of every single thing I'd tried.

Dogs have a layer in their skin made mostly of collagen. It's a wall. When the wall is intact, allergens stay on the outside where they belong.

When the wall breaks down, and it does, especially in dogs over two, gaps form. Pollen slips through. Dust mites burrow in. Grass proteins trigger massive immune responses. The immune system sees invaders and goes into overdrive.

That's the chronic itching. The mutilation. The hot spots. The 2am collar jingling.

And here's where I got angry.

Apoquel suppresses the immune response. Cytopoint blocks the itch signal. Cyclosporine and Zenrelia shut down the immune system more aggressively.

But none of them rebuild the wall.

It's like turning off the smoke alarm while the fire keeps burning. That's why every drug works for three weeks. That's why every drug stops. That's why your vet keeps adding more. The fire is still burning. The wall is still broken. The allergens are still coming through.

I started crying on the bathroom floor at 2am for a different reason. Two years of thinking Henry was a "hard case." Two years of believing I wasn't trying hard enough. None of it was true.

But the next thing I read made me angrier.

Because the article said you CAN rebuild the wall. With collagen. But not the kind of collagen most dog supplements use.

Most dog skin supplements use bovine collagen. Cow collagen. The molecules are over 20,000 Daltons. Way too big for a dog's gut to break down. So you pour it on his food, it goes through his stomach, and it comes out the other end without ever reaching the skin barrier.

You're paying $40, $60, sometimes $80 a bottle for something that physically cannot reach the place it's supposed to fix.

I sell some of these supplements in my grooming salon. I called my distributor on Monday morning and asked them to stop sending three of them.

The only collagen small enough to actually absorb into a dog's skin is marine collagen. From deep sea fish. The peptides are about one tenth the size of bovine. They get through the gut wall. They reach the bloodstream. They reach the skin barrier where the damage actually is.

And it's also 90% Type I, which is the exact type that builds skin and coat. Bovine collagen is mostly Type II, which is for joints. Most dog supplements are giving your dog joint collagen and calling it skin support.

The size is wrong AND the type is wrong.

So I went looking for one that matched the science. And I almost gave up before I found it.

Most products were the bovine kind. The big molecule kind. The kind that wouldn't work.

I finally found one. Marine collagen from deep sea fish. Hydrolyzed peptides under 3,000 Daltons. Dermatologist formulated. Liquid drops on his food once a day. Twenty dollars a bottle. About a dollar a day.

I almost didn't order it. I'd been burned too many times. But I'd just paid $189 for another Cytopoint shot that was going to fail in three weeks. Twenty dollars felt like nothing in comparison.

I clicked buy.

Three weeks later I was crying for a different reason.

The hot spot on his belly that had been there for two months started actually closing. Pink healthy skin where there had been gray.

A week after that he slept through the night without scratching. First time in over a year. I lay in bed listening to nothing and cried because I'd forgotten what nothing sounded like.

A week after that I took the cone off. The fur on the back of his neck started growing back.

A week after that I stopped the Apoquel. I held the four remaining pills in my hand for a long time. Then I put them in the trash. Held my breath for a week.

The itching never came back.

Twelve weeks in I took him for his annual. Different vet this time. She looked at his chart showing no medications in over a month and said "I don't understand. His skin looks healthier than the last time he was here."

I told her about the barrier. About marine collagen. About the size of the molecule.

She read the article on her phone right there in the exam room. "We don't really learn this in vet school. I had no idea the barrier was a factor."

She wasn't defensive. She was curious.

It's been six months. No Apoquel. No Cytopoint. No prescription food. No $400 months. Just one liquid on his food once a day. About a dollar.

Henry runs at the dog park now. His belly is smooth. His coat came back thick and shiny.

If you're where I was, please read what I read. It explains why every medication fails. Why the size of the collagen matters more than the dose. Why your dog might be stuck not because he's a hard case but because the wall is still broken.

It's not a sales page. It's the science that changed everything for me.

pawsorganica.com/products/vet-recommended-itch-relief-drops-new-formula

Your vet isn't wrong. They just weren't taught this.

But now you know.

— Lauren
